chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā and Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The woman with istiḥāḍah looks to her menstrual days, so she does not perform salat in them, and her husband does not approach her. Then when her days have passed and she sees that the blood pierces the cotton, she performs ghusl for ẓuhr and ʿaṣr, delaying this one and hastening that one, and for maghrib and ʿishāʾ one ghusl, delaying this one and hastening that one, and she performs ghusl for ṣubḥ. She places padding, binds herself firmly, and stuffs it, and she joins her thighs in the masjid while the rest of her body is outside. Her husband does not approach her during the days of her menstruation. But if the blood does not pierce the cotton, she performs wudu, enters the masjid, and performs every salat with wudu, and this one her husband may approach except during the days of her hayd.

key_terms.أَيَّامَهَا: her known menstrual days or habitual period
key_terms.اغْتَسَلَتْ: she performs ghusl, the ritual bath
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the masjid, mentioned here in relation to her manner of entry
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, irregular uterine bleeding outside normal menstruation
key_terms.يَثْقُبُ الْكُرْسُفَ: pierces the cotton, indicating heavier bleeding

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings for salat, ghusl, wudu, and marital relations for a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for a woman in istiḥāḍah by distinguishing between her habitual menstrual days and continued non-menstrual bleeding. It explains when she must refrain from salat and marital relations, and when she should perform ghusl or wudu for her prayers depending on the amount of bleeding.
